sections.h2: Which sale route suits an Augusta homeowner?
sections.html:
Three paths are open to a seller in Augusta: an agent-led listing, a private sale, or an as-is purchase by a cash buyer. Condition, calendar and how much of the price you will trade for certainty usually decide it.

  • Agent-led listing: the broadest exposure, with inspection negotiations and a lender's schedule attached.
  • Private sale: you keep the listing fee and take on every task yourself.
  • As-is cash purchase: the fewest moving parts, with an offer that reflects the buyer's own repair and resale costs.

Whichever you pick, Augusta's assessment calendar, its local exemption and Georgia's transfer tax all apply, and the sections below walk through each one.

sections.h2: What makes Augusta unusual among Georgia cities?
sections.html:
Augusta is a consolidated government. The City of Augusta and Richmond County merged on January 1, 1996, and the city calls Augusta-Richmond County one of only three consolidated governments in Georgia. A mayor and ten commissioners govern it, while Hephzibah and Blythe stay independent inside the county lines.

The city lies roughly 150 miles east of Atlanta along Interstate 20, and the Savannah River marks the border with Aiken County, South Carolina. The city's history page says the area around it, the Central Savannah River Area, holds about half a million people. James Oglethorpe founded the settlement in 1736, and Augusta served as Georgia's capital from 1785 to 1795. The 1847 Augusta Canal turned it into a leading inland cotton market, and the city counts nine of its neighborhoods on the federal historic register.

Old neighborhoods mean old houses. If yours stands in a designated historic district, ask the city's Historic Preservation Commission what exterior work needs approval before you spend money on a pre-sale refresh.

sections.h2: Which employers and institutions keep buyers coming to Augusta?
sections.html:
Soldiers, doctors and students supply most of the local demand. The city's own recruiting brochure names Fort Eisenhower (formerly Fort Gordon), NSA Augusta and the Savannah River Site as the core of a cybersecurity and advanced operations cluster.

  • Medical District: Augusta University Health, Piedmont Augusta and the Charlie Norwood VA.
  • Colleges: Augusta University, Augusta Technical College and Paine College, an HBCU.
  • Tournament week: the Masters is played during the first full week of April, which puts the city on national television each spring.

Postings change on a fixed calendar, so owners who receive orders, or who inherit a house from a relative stationed elsewhere, may have only a short runway before a mortgage or vacant-house costs start to hurt.

sections.h2: What does the Census Bureau report for Augusta housing?
sections.html:
The Augusta-Richmond County consolidated government (balance) had an estimated 201,999 people in mid-2025, barely moved from the 202,081 tallied in the 2020 census. Renting and owning split almost evenly, so landlords and tenants make up a large part of the local market.

sections.h2: How does the Richmond County assessment notice and appeal clock work?
sections.html:
Each owner gets a yearly assessment notice in the mail. From the day it is issued, the appeal clock runs 45 days. The notice carries no amount due, and instead shows the assessed value, the exemptions on file and the owner's appeal rights.

The 2026 notices went out June 29, and the city set August 13, 2026 as the last day for appeals and homestead applications on that batch. That deadline has passed, and every year's cutoff is printed on the notice itself. Senate Bill 566 changed the statewide notice layout, so the older tax estimate tables gave way to an Estimated Tax Savings section.

  • File through the Property Search tool at augustarichmondtaxassessor.com, or send the appeal by mail, by email, or in person.
  • Written appeals only, filed before day 45.
  • The Board of Assessors takes questions at 706-821-2310.

Augusta also grants a local floating homestead exemption for qualifying primary residences, limiting certain increases in assessed value. The assessor's FAQ names April 1 as the yearly due date and prints reduced shares for late filers: 66.67% for April 2 through 30, 58.33% during May and 50% on June 1. It adds that bills usually go out in August or September.

sections.h2: What does a seller owe in transfer tax, and how does recording work?
sections.html:
Georgia taxes the transfer itself, using the sale price: $1 covers the first $1,000, then 10 cents for every further $100 or fraction of $100. State revenue guidance puts the liability on the seller, though a contract may hand the cost to the buyer. The Richmond County clerk of superior court will hold the deed unrecorded until the tax is paid.

The reporting form is PT-61, filed through the clerks' cooperative's online portal, and whoever handles your closing usually files it. Ask the tax commissioner what is owed on the current-year bill so the cost can be split between buyer and seller on the settlement statement.

sections.h2: When does a quick as-is sale make sense in Augusta?
sections.html:
A fast sale makes sense when waiting costs more than the discount a cash buyer applies. That discount is real, so collect more than one offer and read every term.

  • An inherited Richmond County house that nobody in the family wants to maintain.
  • A rental with a lease in force, or repairs a lender's appraiser would flag.
  • A move tied to a base or hospital start date that will not shift.
  • A house carrying code violations or liens that make a regular listing difficult.

Request proof of funds, an offer in writing and a fixed closing date from every buyer. The Board of Assessors can also tell you the county's current value for your parcel, which gives you a reference point before any price is quoted.

faqs.q: How many days does an Augusta owner have to contest an assessment?
faqs.a: Forty-five, counted from the day the notice was issued. The 2026 notices were mailed June 29 and the final day was August 13, 2026, which is past. File in writing online, by mail, by email or in person, or call 706-821-2310.

faqs.q: Is Augusta a city or a county?
faqs.a: Both. Augusta and Richmond County merged into one consolidated government in 1996, with Hephzibah and Blythe remaining separate cities inside the county. Ask the tax commissioner which charges appear on your parcel's bill.

faqs.q: Who bears Georgia's transfer tax in an Augusta closing?
faqs.a: By default the seller, though the sales contract can move it to the buyer. Recording waits until it is paid.

faqs.q: Will a cash buyer take an Augusta house with tenants or damage?
faqs.a: Many will, because the purchase is as-is. A regular listing can close with tenants too, but buyers who use loans tend to ask for repairs after an inspection, so compare the money you net from each route.
About 202,000. The mid-2025 estimate is 201,999 for the Augusta-Richmond County consolidated government (balance), and the 2020 census recorded 202,081.
